definition: Unable to be affected, influenced, or passed through by something.
example: The new coating made the old wooden deck impervious to rain and snow.
nuance: Someone impervious to criticism hears it but is not moved by it, while someone oblivious never notices it at all.
prompt: A goalkeeper plays in front of a hostile crowd that jeers at every move.
options: The goalie seemed impervious to the jeers and calmly blocked the next shot.
The impervious goalie bossed his defenders around as if he owned the stadium.
The goalie was so impervious to the jeers that he burst into tears and left the field.
Impervious to the crowd, the goalie changed his stance every time a fan yelled advice.
reasons: Staying steady while the crowd shouts shows the taunts had no effect on him.
Bossy, domineering behavior describes the look-alike imperious, not impervious.
Breaking down shows the jeers hurt him badly, the reverse of being unaffected.
Reacting to every shout means the crowd was influencing him constantly.

practice.prompt: A hiker tests a new rain jacket during a long afternoon downpour.
options: Her impervious jacket kept her shirt completely dry through hours of rain.
Within minutes her impervious jacket was soaked through, and she was shivering.
Lost in a daydream, the impervious hiker never realized it had started to rain.
The impervious hiker rushed up the steep cliff without checking the map or the weather.
reasons: Water could not get through the jacket, which is exactly what the word describes.
A jacket that lets water in right away is the opposite of one that blocks it.
Failing to notice something is being oblivious; this word means resisting what you do notice.
Acting rashly without thinking fits impetuous, a different word that looks similar.
